Volatility is compressing rather than expanding: VIX at 15.52 is 5.31% lower and within 0.10 of its 15.42 session low, and WTI at 91.15 is 1.85% lower after the G7 reserve announcement. That combination describes mean reversion working inside the day's range, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement path the Tail score measures. The published danger window spans 19:00Z to 21:00Z: the current hour carries the Friday power hour into the 20:00Z cash close, and the following futures-only hour runs into the 21:00Z weekly settlement at a record-area level on thinning liquidity. headline: Cash NDX 30,803.53 recovers 66 points off a session low now intact for a third hour, with VIX down 5.31%, holding Tail at 22% into the 20:00Z close
body:
NQ December futures trade 31,034.50 (+274.00, +0.89%) on a quote timed 19:16:33Z, inside a 30,760.25-31,282.25 session range from a 30,771.25 open on about 521.2k contracts, with a 31,042.75/31,043.25 bid/ask. Cash NDX is 30,803.53 (+301.97, +0.99%) on a 19:26:15Z quote against a 30,869.14 open and a 30,501.56 previous close. The defining development of this hour is that the 30,737.07 session low did not give way. It is unchanged from two hours ago, so it has now survived a third hour of trading, and the index has recovered 66.46 points off it rather than pressing it. The index sits 65.61 below its own opening print and 214.00 points, 0.69%, under the 31,017.53 session high.

Volatility and energy both point the same way. VIX is 15.52 (-0.87, -5.31%) on a 19:11:16Z quote against a 16.39 previous close and a 15.42-16.24 session range, so it is pressing the lower end of that range rather than expanding. WTI is 91.15 (-1.72, -1.85%) at 19:16:36Z inside an 88.11-93.51 range, extending its decline after the G7 agreed a coordinated 100 million-barrel crude and diesel release through the IEA over four months, with a front-loaded diesel tranche inside the first twenty days. Both readings subtract from the stress environment rather than adding to it.

The cross-sectional picture is more divided, which is why the dominant mode stays mixed. SMH is 630.81 (+13.00, +2.10%) at 19:26:46Z against a 628.55-636.25 range, holding 2.26 above its low without making a new one. NVDA, by contrast, is 233.89 (+3.02, +1.31%) at 19:26:45Z against a 233.84-237.87 range: it is only 0.05 above a marginal new session low and 1.67% below the 237.87 record intraday high it printed earlier today, when its market capitalisation reached $5.7 trillion. Leadership is leaking into the close even as the index recovers, a narrowing that argues for mixed conditions rather than a one-way path in either direction.

The rate backdrop remains the standing amplifier. The CBOE ten-year yield index is 5.28 (+0.04) on an 18:59:55Z quote against a 5.24 previous close and a 5.16-5.30 session range, so the long end is two basis points below a fresh session high at a level last seen in 2002, and the Federal Reserve H.15 release for 30 September carries the two-year at 4.88%, the ten-year at 5.29% and the thirty-year at 5.64%. That the long end firmed on a day when the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported September nonfarm payrolls up only 29,000 against a 90,000 consensus, unemployment at 4.2% against 4.1% expected and average hourly earnings up 0.1% to $37.81, is the day's most notable dislocation; October rate-hike pricing fell from roughly 64% to 16% on that print while yields still rose.

Tail is therefore held at 22% rather than lifted to the 24% that was published for this hour an hour ago. The forecast's escalation condition was a decisive loss of the cash session low together with a fresh move in the long end, and neither happened. Stress eases one point to 78 on the volatility and energy compression while staying in the high band, and confidence is unchanged at 89 on a complete and current verified evidence set. The shared Finviz context file was read at the start of this run and not used: its collection status is partial and its collection timestamp of 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z is far outside the 90-minute freshness limit, with its calendar and futures sections both recorded as unavailable. Independent research covered that ground instead.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published Claude hours are available, covering the 19:00Z hour on 1 October through the 18:00Z hour today. Tail ran from 20% to 27% across the window. It opened at 20% and held that watch floor for twelve consecutive hours, through the U.S. afternoon on 1 October and the entire Asian session, then stepped to 21% at 07:00Z, 23% at 08:00Z and 22% at 09:00Z as the European-morning advance gained directional efficiency. It returned to 20% for the 10:00Z and 11:00Z hours, then climbed through the payrolls release to 24% at 12:00Z, 25% at 13:00Z and the window peak of 27% at 14:00Z. Those two hours, 13:00Z and 14:00Z, are the only ones in the window published in the block band, and both were published while NQ held within 0.10% of its session extreme with no meaningful pullback. Tail mapped back to 22% for the 15:00Z and 16:00Z hours once a 0.81% retracement was actually observed, lifted to 23% at 17:00Z on a downside-aligned configuration, and eased to 22% at 18:00Z as that configuration stalled. Stress stayed in the high band throughout, between 74% and 79%, and confidence held at 88% or 89% in every hour. The dominant mode was mixed in 20 of the 24 hours, with trend-up recorded only for the 08:00Z and 09:00Z European-morning pair and the 12:00Z to 14:00Z post-payrolls advance.
outlookSummary: The forecast opens at 22% for the current 19:00Z hour, matching the reverted retracement, and steps once to 23% for the 20:00Z slot. That pair is the published danger window: 19:00Z carries the Friday power hour into the 20:00Z cash close, and 20:00Z is a futures-only hour running into the 21:00Z weekly settlement at a record-area level on thinning liquidity. No slot is published in the block band, because the amplifier stack has decayed rather than aligned over the last two hours: the session low held a third time, the index recovered off it, VIX is pressing its session low and oil is falling against the G7 release. The escalation condition on the 20:00Z hour is a decisive loss of the 30,737.07 cash low into the close; a settlement inside Friday's range invalidates it. From 21:00Z the horizon changes character entirely. Weekly settlement prints at 21:00Z and CME Nasdaq-100 futures then halt until 22:00Z on Sunday 4 October, which falls outside this 24-hour window, so every slot from 21:00Z Friday through 18:00Z Saturday is untradable. Those 22 slots are published at the 20% watch floor, which expresses weekend gap exposure carried from the settled level rather than any assumed price structure, since a closed hour cannot produce the repeated extension or failed retracement that Tail measures. Stress decays gradually from 78% to 73% across the weekend as the distance from Friday's realised volatility lengthens, and confidence decays from 89% to 73% purely on the age of the evidence, crossing from the high band into solid in the Saturday afternoon slots. The next scheduled catalysts both sit beyond this horizon: the Sunday reopen, and then ISM Services at 14:00Z on Monday 5 October.
